questions.q: What does the Harvard study cited by Pollan show?
a: More time cooking at home is linked to better health
Home cooking costs more than eating out
Cooking time has no effect on diet
People who cook eat more processed food
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the more time people spend preparing their own food, the better their health tends to be.

questions.q: Why did processed food spread so quickly after World War II?
a: It promised convenience and saved time in the kitchen
It was more nutritious than home cooking
Governments required families to buy it
Fresh ingredients became impossible to find
questions.why: The summary says instant meals were sold as a way to save time, even though they offered little nutritional value.

questions.q: What does fermentation do to bread?
a: It unlocks nutrients the body could not otherwise absorb
It removes most of the grain's fiber
It adds vitamins that were never there
It makes the bread last only a day
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that yeast fermentation releases nutrients in grain that humans cannot digest raw.

questions.q: Which kind of bread does Pollan credit with extra nutritional value?
a: Whole grain bread
White bread
Sourdough bread
Fortified bread
questions.why: The summary notes that white bread lacks the most valuable parts of the grain, unlike whole grain bread.

questions.q: What does the summary say about alcohol in the animal kingdom?
a: Many animals seek out fermented fruit and benefit from it
Animals avoid alcohol because it is toxic to them
Alcohol has no effect on animal behavior
Only primates consume fermented fruit
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes rhinos, tigers and pigs gathering at rotting durian, and flies and rats gaining advantages from alcohol.
